paras: You opened an AI chat, typed in a task from your real week, and got back a paragraph that sounded like a brochure. Maybe you tried it twice. Then you went back to doing the task by hand and decided the people raving about AI were exaggerating.

I spent most of a decade running performance marketing, and I have watched smart, busy people do the same. The tool they tried was good, but the request they gave it was thin, so the answer was thin, and most of them had never been shown how to direct it.

Two professionals can sit in front of the same AI tool with the same task. One gets a generic draft to fix. The other gets a near-final email. The gap between them is a skill, and this page shows you how to build it.
That is why I wrote The Artificial Advantage, and it is why I put this page together.

data.heading: What directing looks like
paras: An example from the book:
A thin request: Write an email to the client about the project delay.

A directed request: Act as a senior account manager at a consulting firm. Write an email to a long-term client explaining that a deliverable they expected Friday will now arrive Tuesday. The delay is due to a data quality issue we caught during QA, something that will improve the final output. The client is detail-oriented and tends to interpret silence as incompetence. The tone should be direct and professional, not apologetic. Open with the updated timeline, explain the reason briefly, and close with what they can expect next. Under 150 words.

What changed: the second prompt tells the AI who is reading, why the delay happened and how that reader takes bad news. The words "not apologetic" do particular work, because without them the AI hedges for a paragraph. The book calls this the Role, Task, Constraint brief, and it is the habit the whole method is built on.

data.heading: Who is writing to you
paras: My name is Elvin Peters. For three years I worked at goeasy, a Canadian lender with two regulated brands, easyfinancial and easyhome, where I ran the paid media myself. The budget was about $1.5M a month, more than $50M in all. Every campaign had to clear a compliance review before it went live, so I learned to be precise about what I asked for and careful about what I accepted.
After that I advised large advertisers at an ad tech company. In 2026 I became a founder, writing books and building with AI full time.

data.heading: What you get, and what each piece does for you
paras: 1. The Artificial Advantage, the 2026 edition ebook. Fourteen chapters in three parts, built around CLEAR: Choose your tools, Lead with clear direction, Evolve your outputs, Audit for accuracy, and Repeat to build a practice. Part 1 gets you past the hesitation. Part 2 shows you how to choose a tool and a mode for the job, so you stop getting a fifty-page strategy document when you needed ten slides. Chapter 8 covers that, and you can read it free here. Part 3 is the core skill: the three rules for beginners, how to take a first draft to a final one, and how to read an AI answer critically before your name goes on it. Along the way you brief AI with Role, Task, Constraint, so the first answer is close to what you meant, and you check an answer with the Two-Step Verification Method before you use it. When an answer comes back wrong, the Diagnostic Ladder traces it to its cause, so you fix the request instead of starting over. Your first assignment is to pick one task you do every week and dread, and run it through the method. Chapter 14, the last in Part 3, turns the method into a practice you keep.

2. The Toolkit: the method in files you can edit. Every exercise, prompt and role from the book, already typed into Word documents, so the practice starts the day you open it rather than after an evening of copying things out.

• Twenty-five prompts for the tasks that eat your week, each one already carrying the role, the task and the limits. Paste, fill in your details, and the job starts. They come as a spreadsheet too, for import into whatever you already use.
  • Twenty-five role setups you paste once, so the AI answers as someone who knows your field, with the formula for writing your own.
  • Sixteen exercises from ten chapters, each run on your own work, with a record of what happened.
  • A 30-day plan and a 3-month plan, from your first real task to saved workflows you reuse.
  • A 12-job tool guide, so you look up the job and see which kind of tool fits.

3. The Companion Library, online, kept current. Everything in the book you would otherwise flip back to, on a page that opens from the code printed in the book (the ebook included), on any screen, with no email and no login. The Prompt Builder assembles a correct brief from three answers, the Quick Reference Card puts the method on one page, and the tools reference is updated as the tools change, so the book does not go stale on your shelf.

4. The 7-Day AI Workbook. Seven days, one real task of your own. You run it the old way on Day 2 and save the result. You run it through the full method on Day 7 and compare. You finish the week with a before, an after, and a template you keep, which means by next Friday you have proof in your own work that the method holds.

5. Everything AI 2026. When a new job lands on your desk, you look it up and see the tools that fit and what each costs, instead of reading reviews. A reference of 684 AI tools organised by job, as a spreadsheet and a PDF field guide.

6. The 12 Commandments to Make AI Obey. Twenty-two pages of habits for the free and basic plans of ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Grok, with two starter files you fill in once: an About Me file, so you stop re-typing who you are in every chat, and a voice file, so the drafts sound like you.

data.alt: Workbook page 4, Day 1: The Director's Mindset. It shows today's skill, a short note on taking the director's chair, and the start of the Task Card with lines to fill in: the task in one sentence, who it is for, and what done looks like.

items.q: Do I need a paid AI plan?
items.a: No. The book teaches skills that carry across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot. You can start on a free plan.

The book was written for professionals who tried AI and shrugged, and for people whose company just told them to use it. If you already use AI daily, the Diagnostic Ladder and the verification method are the chapters most likely to help.
The ebook, the Toolkit that comes with the book, the 7-Day AI Workbook, and the Companion Library. The price box on this page is the live list from the store.

items.a: Digital downloads, available right after checkout, and nothing is shipped.
